Examples · the models in use

Worked examples

CPDSE-teachers use the three models in two main kinds of work. These examples show one of each: a real course, and an imagined workshop for the teachers of a real course.

Curriculum courses
Courses in the pharmacy and pharmaceutical-science programmes at SDU and UCPH that CPDSE helps upgrade or create, so students meet modern pharmaceutical data science.
People Development
Learning for people already in post: researchers, educators, and technical or administrative staff. It includes the FrAIday Bar, a one-hour hands-on session every second Friday, the informal Vibe Café straight after, and tailored workshops built around a group's own work.

Both courses are real and link to their official descriptions. The workshop, starting levels, targets and session designs are illustrative, not assessments of real students or staff.

  • Curriculum course · FA516 course

    Chemical and pharmaceutical data science

    Students learn how chemical and pharmaceutical data are represented and analysed: molecular descriptors, machine learning for property prediction, model evaluation and reproducible notebooks. The course ends with a group project on a real dataset.

    Anchor
    Lead Optimisation & Candidate Selection
    Targets Illustrative
    Model assessment and sensitivity analysis L1→L3; Reproducible Analysis L2→L3
    Deliver Illustrative
    One two-hour exercise session (120 minutes), one of about 15

  • People Development · SMPS20003U teachers' workshop

    Workshop for the teachers of Methods and Procedures in Clinical Drug Development

    In this real course, students write a clinical-trial protocol from a medical case. This imagined People Development workshop helps the course's teachers mark the statistics in those protocols and judge how students use AI tools.

    Anchor
    Phase I / II / III
    Targets Illustrative
    Hypothesis testing L2→L3; What can AI be used for? What can it not be used for? L1→L2
    Deliver Illustrative
    First half-day of two (120 minutes)

Worksheet: place your own course or workshop

Work through these prompts on paper or in a shared document. They follow the same order as the examples.

  1. Anchor

    Which substep, or at most two, does the course prepare people for? Browse the value chain and note the primary data-science question.

  2. Assess and target

    Pick two or three competencies in the competence model. For each, write today's typical level and a realistic target. The level rubric helps you decide.

  3. Deliver

    Sketch one session as a 4Cs sequence, one block for each C: how people connect, a short concept input, hands-on practice, and how they conclude. Check each block against the Six Trumps.

Print this page to get the prompts on paper.
